si.qualification_scope: Release-reported selected corpus and release engineer scoring. Residual semantic errors exist; not independent external review. Not a latency guarantee. Separate from synthetic site demonstration.

da.scope: Release-reported reference log; external production log, Python 3.12 qualification and signed OCI not established. No end-to-end guarantee.

native_lineage_example.scope: controlled synthetic source assertions; pending disclosure approval
native_lineage_example.limits: No established transaction identity, settlement, discharge or operative authority.

verification_scope.contract: Exact original native store and response recheck; browser projection and report binding only; publisher authentication NOT VERIFIED
verification_scope.lineage: Fresh replay reproduced candidate source-linked output; established same-transaction identity not demonstrated
verification_scope.da: Fresh isolated mock execution and historical packet verification; V16 NOT RUN

buyer_positioning.company: Two independently licensable enterprise infrastructure runtimes; evidence-qualified meaning and exact-action permission-to-act are separate responsibilities.

si.private_core: Completely offline, CPU, no LLM, internet, GPU or cloud AI required; air-gapped with locally provisioned dependencies. Optional providers are not authority.

differentiation.description: Every visible constituted concept must have a real semantic identity, a definition, a domain, a category, standing and exact supporting source evidence. This is more than extracting names or generating plausible descriptions.
differentiation.potential_buyer_value: Reduce time spent tracing definitions and explaining decisions to data owners and auditors.

differentiation.description: Competing meanings, uncertain classifications and unresolved conflicts stay visible. Business and technical concepts coexist without collapsing different senses or treating absence of evidence as false.
differentiation.potential_buyer_value: Avoid silently propagating inconsistent definitions into reports, models and agents.

differentiation.capability: Business obligations, not just field names
differentiation.description: The finance-first, domain-extensible model captures who owes what, to whom, under what conditions, with relevant amount, currency, time, lifecycle and lineage when supported. A source assertion is not legal discharge or authority.
differentiation.potential_buyer_value: Make contract, lending, payments and other operational information more usable without manufacturing facts.

differentiation.description: What a source says, what it means, and what is actually in force or authorized are separate. Unknown settlement or fulfillment stays unknown until appropriate evidence exists.
differentiation.potential_buyer_value: Prevent a status label from becoming an unsupported business conclusion.

differentiation.description: Generate native semantic data contracts for eligible fields from a sealed revision. Strict validation, receipts, staleness and drift checks distinguish a changed definition from an unchanged physical data type.
differentiation.potential_buyer_value: Catch meaning changes before they flow silently into downstream reporting or integrations.

differentiation.description: A governed semantic asset drives UI, API and export projections. Qualified input profiles and all 17 output formats, with release-reported cross-format parity checks, make the meaning reusable.
differentiation.potential_buyer_value: Reuse the asset across existing catalog, graph, BI and application tools rather than rebuilding maps for each consumer.

differentiation.capability: Permission bound to the exact action
differentiation.description: Bind the actor, operation, target and material parameters—not a broad approval, token or model score. Changing a material amount, recipient or target invalidates the earlier binding.
differentiation.potential_buyer_value: Reduce exposure to substituted or manipulated payments, record changes and privileged tool calls.

differentiation.description: Use controlled policy, authority, evidence and current resource state rather than claims supplied by an agent. Keep the actual business decision with its authorized human or system owner.
differentiation.potential_buyer_value: Keep existing approvals and accountability intact across agentic workflows.

differentiation.description: An earlier ALLOW is not permanent permission. Re-evaluate current conditions at the protected execution point; missing or changed required authority is refused or routed for review.
differentiation.potential_buyer_value: Close the gap between approval and execution when circumstances change.

differentiation.capability: Fail closed at the protected boundary
differentiation.description: A trusted executor verifies the exact signed, anchored consume acknowledgement before a protected effect. A decision endpoint alone is not enforcement; all relevant routes must be controlled for the desired protection.
differentiation.potential_buyer_value: Make the wrong action fail at the route that matters, not just generate an alert.

differentiation.description: Idempotent retry, reconciliation and explicit unresolved outcomes distinguish a consumed authorization from an observed effect. Missing receipt evidence is not treated as no effect.
differentiation.potential_buyer_value: Support incident investigation and recovery without turning an ambiguous retry into a new business action.

differentiation.description: Correlate authorization, pre-effect consume, reasons and a separate signed outcome. Portable packets and a standalone verifier support verification without trusting the live runtime; independent production log and pinned trust are deployment requirements.
differentiation.potential_buyer_value: Give audit, risk and customer teams a defensible approval-to-effect record within the covered route.

da.public_proof_scope: Reviewed adapter and bounded software harness only; no customer deployment or production-wide non-bypassability.

buyer_positioning.commercial_scope: Potential buyer value, not guaranteed ROI. Enterprise and OEM licensing; focused paid evaluations with buyer-owned inputs and protected route.

public_disclosure: Public product behavior and scoped synthetic outputs only. Detailed runtime source, implementation, API contracts and private diligence materials are not distributed.
